name: Mount Sturgeon

facts.claim: Mt Sturgeon (Wurgarri) Walk is a listed walk in Grampians (Gariwerd) National Park, with its own trailhead
The mount behind Dunkeld, at the southern end of the Grampians; the town was first called Mount Sturgeon
The Grampians Peaks Trail finishes at Dunkeld in the south

name: Silverband Falls

facts.claim: Horsetail falls fed by Dairy Creek in Grampians National Park; a narrow band of water tumbles over a small rock face and vanishes into a rocky base
Easy stroll along a fern-laden trail in the Wonderland Range, with birdlife such as yellow robins and wedge-tailed eagles
The creek re-emerges about 50 m west of the falls

name: Halls Gap

facts.claim: Town in the Fyans Valley at the foot of the Wonderland and Mount William ranges, on Grampians Road beside the national park; about 3 hours from Melbourne
Home to Brambuk, Australia's longest running Aboriginal cultural centre
Halls Gap Zoo is 7 km from town
Grampians Peaks Trail passes through Halls Gap

name: Dunkeld

facts.claim: Town at the southern end of Grampians National Park, about 283 km west of Melbourne on the Glenelg Highway
Has a local museum, art gallery, bakery, cafes and a tourist information centre
The Grampians Peaks Trail finishes at Dunkeld

facts.claim: Founded 1853 as Pleasant Creek in the gold rush; one of few Victorian towns with active gold mining, 237 km west-north-west of Melbourne
Famed for the Stawell Gift, a professional footrace begun in 1878
Known as the gateway to Grampians National Park; Bunjil's Shelter rock art is about 10 km south
